title: Platform systems & services — comprehensive runbook, dashboards and roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Platform team’s systems & services inventory, operational runbooks, dashboard and alerting standards, on-call procedures, retrospective cadence and the roadmap for Q2 2026. It is intended as the canonical runbook for level 1/2 triage and for platform engineers onboarding to system ownership.

Scope
- Applies to services owned by eng-platform: redwood-api-gw, inference-runtime, kv-cache-service, router-proxy, metrics-collector, auth-frontier.
- Excludes customer-specific private deployments (see eng-private-deployments reference docs).

Owner & Contacts
- Platform lead / owner: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.example.com)
- On-call rota owner: Liam O'Connor (liam@redwood.example.com)
- Pager escalation: SRE Escalation Team (pager: +1-555-0101)
- Slack channels: #platform-oncall, #platform-ops, #infra-retros

Systems & Services inventory (summary)
| Service | Purpose | Primary Owner | SLO (p95) | Notes |
| redwood-api-gw | Public API ingress & rate limiting | Platform API team | p95 < 150ms | edge + auth integration |
| inference-runtime | Model inference serving (hosted) | Serving runtime team | p95 < 250ms, error rate < 0.5% | autoscale by qps and GPU slots |
| kv-cache-service | Prefix and KV caching for sessions | Platform caching team | p99 < 50ms | local LRU, multi-tenant quotas |
| router-proxy | Smart routing & fallback | Platform routing team | p95 < 100ms | routing policies by region/tier |
| metrics-collector | Telemetry ingestion pipeline | Observability team | ingestion latency < 30s | backs up to long-term storage |

Standard runbook template (use for every service page)
1. Summary: short description + high-level architecture diagram link.
2. Ownership: primary, secondary, pager.
3. SLO/SLA and key metrics to watch.
4. Common failure modes and diagnostic commands.
5. Immediate mitigation steps (page-level).
6. Post-incident tasks and retro link.

Example: inference-runtime — triage checklist (level 1)
1. Check overall health: kubectl get pods -n inference | grep -v Running (or Grafana panel).
2. Check model-queue length and GPU utilization (grafana -> Inference / Runtime -> GPU Utilization).
3. Validate recent deploys: open the last rollout in ArgoCD and check for failures.
4. Confirm dependent services: redis (cache), s3 (model artifacts), metrics-collector.
5. If p95 latency > 500ms and error rate > 1% for 5m -> page primary oncall.

Immediate mitigation steps (ordered)
1. Scale a) increase replica count for the service (kubectl scale deploy inference-runtime --replicas=N) OR b) trigger autoscale override in the console.
2. If GPU contention suspected, move low-priority jobs to best-effort queue.
3. If model artifact load is failing, revert to previous model version using pinned tag in deployment config.
4. For traffic spikes, enable circuit-breaker to route 20% of traffic to a smaller, lower-latency model variant (router-proxy policy).
5. For persistent errors, fail over traffic to Dedicated cluster (see failover runbook: related_pages).

Dashboards & alerting standards
- Dashboards: all services must have a Grafana dashboard with the following panels: latency (p50/p95/p99), success rate, qps, resource utilization (CPU/GPU/Memory), rollout status.
- Naming convention: team.service.panel (e.g., platform.inference-runtime.latency).
- Alerting: alerts must be actionable, paged only when human intervention likely to change outcome. Use severity labels: P1 (page), P2 (slack notify), P3 (ticket).

Key alerting thresholds (defaults — tune by service)
- P1 page: p95 latency > 300ms for 5 min OR error_rate > 1.0% for 3 min OR SLO burn rate > 10x for 5 min.
- P2 slack: sustained increase in background errors (e.g., 0.2% < error_rate < 1.0%) OR high CPU/GPU > 85% for 10 min.
- P3 ticket: single-host disk > 80% or ingestion lag > 60s.

Alert definitions should include: symptom, affected scope, runbook link, suggested pager. Avoid noisy alerts: use a 5m evaluation window and penalties for flapping (notify-after: 3 occurrences within 10m).

Dashboard example (panels to create)
1. Service overview: p50/p95/p99 latency, qps, success rate.
2. Resource trends: CPU, memory, GPU util %, GPU memory pressure.
3. Queueing: request queue length, backlog, KV cache hit ratio.
4. Upstream/downstream: API gateway latency to service, downstream storage errors.
5. Recent deploys & rollout status.

How-to: create a service dashboard (step-by-step)
1. Clone platform-template-dashboard in Grafana.
2. Replace datasource queries with service-specific metrics (metric prefixes: platform.<service>.*).
3. Configure alert rules in Prometheus using the platform-alerting repo: apply alerts/*.yaml -> kubectl apply -f alerts/<service>-alerts.yaml.
4. Add dashboard to /ops/dashboards repo and create a PR referencing owner and reviewers.

CI/CD & deploy runbook notes
- Standard deploys use ArgoCD with automated promotion for canary -> stable.
- Canary rollout policy: 10% for 10m -> 50% for 20m -> 100% if no regressions.
- If rollout fails: abort canary, rollback to previous stable tag with argo rollback <app> <rev>.

On-call escalation matrix (summary)
1. Primary platform oncall (P1): page primary owner. 5 minutes after page with no ack -> page secondary.
2. 15 minutes after unresolved and no mitigation -> page platform lead.
3. 30 minutes after unresolved -> page SRE leadership and open an incident channel #incident-<id>.

Post-incident process & retrospectives
- Create incident in Incident tracker template (link in templates folder). Add: summary, start/end, impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, remediation plan, owner, timeline.
- Postmortem timeline: draft within 48h, final within 7 days.
- Retro cadence: monthly ops retro to review top 5 incidents, action tracker to be owned by the platform lead.
- Blameless questions to answer: what happened? what were the enabling conditions? what detection gaps existed? what experiments can reduce recurrence?

Platform roadmap — Q2 2026 highlights
- Reliability: reduce inference-runtime p95 by 20% through kernel selection improvements and smarter routing (owner: serving-runtime).
- Observability: roll out distributed tracing for inference calls end-to-end (owner: observability team).
- Cost & efficiency: implement adaptive batching strategies and a trial quantization profile for popular open models (owner: optimize).
- On-call ergonomics: reduce noisy alerts by 50% through alert triage project (owner: eng-platform).

Operational hygiene & runbook lifecycle
- Every service must review runbook and alerts quarterly.
- Runbook owner responsible for: runbook accuracy, dashboard coverage, and at least one runbook drill per quarter.
- Runbook changes require a reviewer from SRE and the service owner.

Appendices
- Useful CLI snippets:
  - kubectl rollout status deploy/<service> -n <ns>
  - kubectl logs -f deploy/<service> -n <ns> --tail=200
  - argo rollouts promote <app>
- Useful dashboards: /grafana/d/platform-template-dashboard
- Playbook templates and incident checklist: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/templates

Related pages

- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template
